look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Find the upright, narrow spore-bearing pair of basal pinnae that rises above the broad green sterile part of the frond. These are fertile fern leaf divisions, NOT flowers. Check the straw-colored stalk and once-pinnate blade with 4–7 pairs of mostly lanceolate pinnae.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Terrestrial fern of lightly shaded limestone rock habitats; fronds arise along a creeping rhizome, rather than from a single tight crown.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Sterile green blade roughly triangular to lanceolate and once pinnate, typically 4–7 pairs of lanceolate pinnae with finely serrulate edges; straw-colored petiole.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Ferns have no flowers or seeds. Sporangia are concentrated on a distinctive erect pair of narrow fertile pinnae near the base of the blade; these can project above the sterile blade.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: No fruit or seed; examine mature sporangia and ridged spores on fertile pinnae.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Creeping rhizome with dark hairs; inspect the long straw-colored frond stalk.
